input: Azure Machine Learning batch endpoints run long-lived asynchronous inference jobs over files stored in Azure Storage. The workshop uses a pipeline component deployment so each execution preserves inputs, outputs, logs, identity context, and MLflow metrics for later comparison.

Azure API Management exposes multiple independently allocated embedding deployments through one stable endpoint. A weighted backend pool distributes requests, while managed identity removes model API keys from the Azure Machine Learning job and from workshop configuration files.

Document ingestion divides source files into retrieval chunks before embedding. Smaller chunks improve retrieval precision but increase the number of logical embedding operations, which can make request or call-rate limits visible before all assigned token capacity is consumed.

Packing combines compatible text chunks into the input array accepted by the Azure OpenAI embeddings API. It reduces client HTTP requests while retaining one input identifier for every returned vector index, making output correlation testable after asynchronous execution.

Token-aware packing applies both an item ceiling and a token ceiling. The item ceiling respects the service array limit, while the operational token ceiling derives from assigned deployment capacity, desired utilization, and the planned request cadence.

Tokens per minute and requests per minute are paired when Azure quota is allocated, but Azure evaluates token pressure and request pressure separately during inference. Either limiter can return HTTP 429, so status code alone does not identify the cause.

A clean capacity experiment uses the same model version, text distribution, packing limits, retry policy, and observation window for direct and pooled routes. Changing several variables at once would prevent a defensible attribution of the measured throughput difference.

MLflow metrics are written on the Azure Machine Learning child command job. Attempted and successful rates, accepted prompt tokens, latency percentiles, throttle counts, and packing-fill ratios provide run-level evidence without storing source text or embedding vectors in telemetry.

An API Management circuit breaker observes configured backend failures and temporarily removes an unhealthy backend from selection. After the trip duration the circuit resets, allowing requests to resume while the application continues using eligible pool members.

Short burst rates can exceed assigned per-minute capacity because the denominator covers only a few seconds. Sustained conclusions require paced runs over clean quota windows, repeated measurements, low throttle rates, and explicit separation of service contracts from empirical observations.
